title: Temporal Preferences in Language Models for Long-Horizon Assistance

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating intertemporal choices by prompting models to select between smaller-sooner (SS) and larger-later (LL) monetary rewards to measure delay discounting and future-oriented versus present-oriented preferences.
Applying persona prompts with male and female identities to measure if the model's delay discounting behavior and temporal preferences change based on assigned gender.
Prompting models with different regional identities (Iran, USA, Europe) to observe if geographic and socio-political contexts influence the model's intertemporal choice decisions.
Assigning the model a specific occupational/legal role (e.g., 'Finance minister') to assess if professional context alters its preference for immediate versus delayed rewards.
